plan.summary: BRO-5549: checked the owner’s second batch of Gemini deep research (nonprofit pipeline 2023-25, 2023-24 season, 2024-25 season) at source. New records: The Band’s Visit ($8.75M, recouped after 11 months; Broadway News, matches its Form D) and The Play That Goes Wrong ($4M, recouped after 17 months, about $305K weekly operating expenses; Broadway News). SEC Form D figures: Redwood $16M (was ~$15M, unsourced), Call Me Izzy $4,725,000 (was ~$4.9M, unsourced). Once Upon a Mattress stays an estimate, now ~$7.5M from a Form D that does not name the show. Rejected: the Halcyon Theatricals enhancement claims (the company launched Feb 2026, after all six shows), The Wiz $5.6M (Giant’s figure), Lempicka $16M (uncited); Gypsy’s weekly cost lead is a Reddit post this container cannot open.

entry.capitalizationSource: Broadway News (Sep 10, 2018): "“The Band’s Visit” has recouped its $8.75 million capitalization after 11 months on Broadway, the producers announced Monday." https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-bands-visit-recoups-after-11-months-on-broadway/ The SEC Form D (Band’s Visit Broadway, LLC, filed May 15, 2017) gives the same total offering amount, $8,750,000. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1705879/000170587917000001/xslFormDX01/primary_doc.xml
entry.recoupedSource: Broadway News (Sep 10, 2018): "“The Band’s Visit” has recouped its $8.75 million capitalization after 11 months on Broadway, the producers announced Monday." https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-bands-visit-recoups-after-11-months-on-broadway/
entry.notes: Began off-Broadway at the Atlantic Theater Company. Recouped its $8.75 million capitalization after 11 months, announced Sep 10, 2018 (Broadway News); won 10 Tony Awards including Best Musical. No weekly running cost reported.

actions.description: the-bands-visit-2017: no commercial record yet; Broadway News reports the recoupment of its $8.75M capitalization (matches its SEC Form D). Windfall: recouped, model investor multiple 1.34x-1.76x (central 1.57x) against the 1.5x line.

entry.capitalizationSource: Broadway News (Aug 21, 2018): "“The Play That Goes Wrong” has recouped its $4 million capitalization, 17 months after it began performances on Broadway." https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-play-that-goes-wrong-recoups-its-4-million-investment/
entry.recoupedSource: Broadway News (Aug 21, 2018): "“The Play That Goes Wrong” has recouped its $4 million capitalization, 17 months after it began performances on Broadway." https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-play-that-goes-wrong-recoups-its-4-million-investment/
entry.weeklyRunningCostSource: Broadway News (Aug 21, 2018): "Across about one year of performances, the play’s weekly operating expenses averaged about $305,000, according to documents filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission." https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-play-that-goes-wrong-recoups-its-4-million-investment/
entry.notes: Produced by Kevin McCollum, J.J. Abrams and Kenny Wax. Recouped its $4 million capitalization 17 months after it began performances (Broadway News, Aug 2018), helped by low running costs: weekly operating expenses averaged about $305,000 over about a year, per SEC filings. Extended its run to Jan 6, 2019.

actions.description: the-play-that-goes-wrong-2017: no commercial record yet; Broadway News reports the recoupment of its $4M capitalization and its average weekly operating expenses from SEC filings (an all-in figure). Trickle: recouped late in a 22-month run.
